symptom: Every signed-in cloud save fails. api/profile returns 502 with detail provider_rejected_server_key; the provider answers 401 to the server's own credential. Sign-in, sessions, reads and every gate are unaffected — only authoritative writes.
measuredBy: GET /api/health?deep=1, which asks the provider directly and answers in booleans.
eliminated: A stale build. The value was updated, a fresh deployment was made afterwards, and the result is unchanged. An environment variable binds at build time, and Vercel skips a SHA it has already built, so this had to be ruled out first.
A different project on each side. SUPABASE_URL and VITE_SUPABASE_URL resolve to the same project ref, so the credential is being shown to the right door.
A missing or misnamed variable. SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY is present and correctly shaped, which is precisely why every earlier check reported the system ready.
The browser credential. Anonymous sign-in still issues sessions, so the publishable key is valid for this project.
A defect in the probe. An independent real save through the product's own server path returned the same 401 before this probe existed.
A permissions problem. A 401 with no PostgREST code comes from the gateway, before PostgREST is reached. A grant or RLS problem would be 403 with a code such as 42501.
A probe pointed at the wrong path. That would be 404, which the probe deliberately does not treat as a refusal.
A masked paste. looksLikeSecretKey() rejects any non-printable character, and the value passes, so it is not the bullet-masked copy that bit this project once before.
Scoping to one environment. The owner set the variable for all environments and two further rebuilds followed.
remaining: The string in SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY is well formed and starts the right way, but this project does not recognise it. Two ways that happens: it is an older secret key that has since been revoked, or it is a valid secret key belonging to a DIFFERENT Supabase project. The URL check only proves the server and browser agree on which project to call; it cannot tell whether the key was issued by that project.
ownerAction: Open the Supabase project whose ref is lfybiphmqkiecfrqsfzt. If more than one project exists on the account, this is the one, and a key from any other project will fail exactly like this.
Project Settings then API Keys. Copy the current secret key, the one beginning sb_secret_. If several are listed, take the newest and revoke the rest afterwards.
Paste it into Vercel as SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY for all environments, then redeploy.
productImpact: None beyond the save itself, and the failure is honest: the postgame panel says the save failed, the result stays on screen, and nothing is simulated again. Guest play is unaffected and no data is lost.
howItWillBeConfirmed: GET /api/health?deep=1 reports serverCredentialAccepted: true and serverCredentialProbeStatus: 200.
